title: Cork to New Zealand
standfirst: This later family moved from a documented Scottish starting point to County Cork, with descendants later in New Zealand. Its historical connection to the Ulster locality clusters has not been found.
question: Is there any documentary bridge from this Cork family to an earlier Glasgow branch?
answer: No current evidence joins this Cork–New Zealand family to the Ulster clusters. A broad surname or project-level Y-DNA affinity cannot replace a documented historical connection.

chapters.title: A Scottish starting point
body: Alexander Glasgow's profile reports a Barony baptism in 1792 and a 1826 Glasgow marriage to Ellen Smith.
The maintained notes have not yet assessed the underlying record images, so these profile details remain leads to verify rather than a bridge to another Glasgow family.

chapters.title: The Cork estate
body: The profile material places Alexander at Oldcourt, County Cork, after its 1852 purchase, and reports a Carrigaline holding in Griffith's Valuation.
These reported Cork facts define a later local family study; they do not identify an earlier Irish parent generation.

chapters.title: A line kept independent
body: Later descendants reached New Zealand, but the supplied evidence does not provide a chain back from Cork into Ulster.
The family is therefore presented beside the Ulster studies, not inside any of them.
